knowledge:
- key_parameters: wells=A list or data frame of droplet amplitudes (e.g., KRASdata) or a directory path containing amplitude CSV files ;; cMethod=The classification method to use or plot (e.g., "Cluster", "thresholds", "kmeans", "kmeansMahRain", "knn", "grid", "kmeansSdRain") ;; ch1Threshold=Linear amplitude threshold for Channel 1 ;; ch2Threshold=Linear amplitude threshold for Channel 2 ;; maxDistances=The maximum Mahalanobis distance from cluster centers, specified as a single value or a named list for each cluster (NN, NP, PN, PP) ;; errorLevel=Standard deviation multiplier for rain filtering, specified as a named list for each cluster ;; trainData=A data frame of droplet amplitudes used as the training set for k-NN classification ;; cl=A vector of classifications for the training set ;; k=The number of nearest neighbors to consider in k-NN classification
- alternatives: thresholdClassify=Simple linear gating, but subjective and less accurate for leaning or lifting clusters ;; kmeansClassify=Fast, automated clustering, but requires knowing the number of clusters and works best when all wells are classified together to avoid empty cluster issues ;; knnClassify=Uses a clean training set to classify the rest of the plate, which is useful when k-means struggles with noise ;; gridClassify=Manual corner-based gating, which is tedious but useful if clusters have very clear separation but standard algorithms fail ;; mahalanobisRain=Rain filtering that respects the elliptical shape of clusters, whereas sdRain uses standard deviation thresholds along the axes ;; shinyVisApp=A Shiny-based GUI alternative for non-R users
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing two-channel droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) data to classify droplets, filter out ambiguous "rain" droplets, and calculate target DNA concentrations using Poisson statistics.
- pitfalls: Running k-means on individual wells can fail if some wells have empty clusters; it is highly recommended to classify all wells in a plate together ;; Default maxDistances=3 in mahalanobisRain can be too strict and classify too many valid droplets as rain; fine-tuning using a named list (e.g., list(NN=35, NP=35, PN=35, PP=35)) is often necessary ;; File reading errors ("duplicate 'row.names' are not allowed") can occur if the header row column count differs from data rows (e.g., trailing commas/tabs in CSVs) ;; Custom classifications must be formatted as a factor with exact levels: c("NN", "NP", "PN", "PP", "Rain", "N/A")

workflows.name: standard_kmeans_mahalanobis
workflows.intent: Load raw ddPCR amplitude data, classify droplets using k-means, apply Mahalanobis distance-based rain filtering, and generate a Poisson concentration summary.
input: data/amplitudes (directory containing raw droplet amplitude CSV files exported from QuantaSoft)
workflows.stages: 1. Load raw amplitude data into a ddpcrPlate object ;; 2. Classify droplets using the k-means algorithm ;; 3. Apply Mahalanobis distance-based rain filtering with customized cluster distances ;; 4. Generate a Poisson concentration summary
workflows.code:
plate <- ddpcrPlate(wells=KRASdata)
plate <- kmeansClassify(plate)
plate <- mahalanobisRain(plate, cMethod="kmeans", maxDistances=list(NN=35, NP=35, PN=35, PP=35))
kmeansMahRainSummary <- plateSummary(plate, cMethod="kmeansMahRain")
head(kmeansMahRainSummary)

workflows.name: knn_classification
workflows.intent: Classify ddPCR droplets using the k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) algorithm trained on a clean subset of wells.
input: data/amplitudes (directory containing raw droplet amplitude CSV files exported from QuantaSoft)
workflows.stages: 1. Load raw amplitude data ;; 2. Subset specific wells to create a clean training plate ;; 3. Classify the training plate using k-means and remove noise with Mahalanobis rain ;; 4. Extract the clean training set using removeDropletClasses ;; 5. Classify the full plate using knnClassify with the training set
workflows.code:
plate <- ddpcrPlate(wells=KRASdata)
trainWells <- plate[c("E03", "A04")]
trainPlate <- ddpcrPlate(wells=trainWells)
trainPlate <- kmeansClassify(trainPlate)
trainPlate <- mahalanobisRain(trainPlate, cMethod="kmeans", maxDistances=3)
trainSet <- removeDropletClasses(trainPlate, cMethod="kmeansMahRain")
trainSet <- do.call(rbind, trainSet)
trainAmplitudes <- trainSet[, c("Ch1.Amplitude", "Ch2.Amplitude")]
trainCl <- trainSet$kmeansMahRain
plate <- knnClassify(plate, trainData=trainAmplitudes, cl=trainCl, k=3)
